label: Applied Khaldunian historical sociology to dismantle patriarchal hadith memory
description: Working inside the Maghrebi sociological tradition traced to Ibn Khaldun, Mernissi examined how state power, tribal politics (asabiyyah), and Umayyad/Abbasid elites reshaped religious memory and gender spatial boundaries.
dialecticalTension: Turns historical-materialist historiography toward critical hadith and gender analysis.
historicalContext: Beyond the Veil (1975) and The Veil and the Male Elite (1987).

citations.author: Fatema Mernissi
citations.work: The Veil and the Male Elite

label: Opened historical-critical Islamic feminism foundational to Wadud's Qur'anic method
description: Mernissi's demonstration that patriarchal biases entered Islamic orthodoxy through post-prophetic historical transmission paved the methodological path for Amina Wadud's holistic gender-egalitarian Qur'anic hermeneutics.
dialecticalTension: Shifts from critiquing male hadith chains to reconstructing systematic Qur'anic hermeneutics.
historicalContext: 1987–1992 emergence of transnational Islamic feminist philosophy.

citations.author: Ziba Mir-Hosseini
citations.work: Muslim Women's Quest for Equality: Between Islamic Law and Feminism

label: Critiqued modernist Islamic feminism's reliance on liberal-autonomous subject norms
description: While honoring Mernissi's scholarship, Saba Mahmood scrutinized reformist assumptions that Muslim women's flourishing can only be measured by resistance to traditional piety, highlighting instead embodied ethical cultivation.
dialecticalTension: Debates whether Islamic agency requires liberating scriptural modernity or non-liberal habituation.
historicalContext: Politics of Piety (2005) engagement with Muslim feminist historiography.
